findings.anchor: rk-essex-1 explanation last clause EN/FA vs DE
findings.observed: DE says no blanket resection rule, whereas EN/FA specifically deny a blanket prohibition of resection. In the confirmed longitudinal-instability context the unnecessary extra negation is both non-equivalent and potentially confusing after correctly teaching radial-length preservation.
findings.required: Remove this final resection-negation clause uniformly, retaining the existing individualized fixation/replacement and essential radial-length preservation/restoration statements.

findings.anchor: RADIUSKOPF_LESSON Mason rows and take-home thresholds/fragmentation versus revised original pool
findings.observed: The pool now explicitly teaches a descriptive partial-head/whole-head distinction and Johnston extension; retained lesson text still foregrounds PDF numerical thresholds and III multi-fragmentation. The PDF itself does contain the old numerical summary; the issue is the still-pending explanatory bridge between versions, not a false statement that the PDF says something else.
findings.required: Complete the author-planned bounded teaching-table/summary alignment and source/version explanation, then request actual after-value retest. Do not erase PDF provenance or turn morphology into automatic treatment.

scienceJudgment: No wrong key, DE/EN/FA polarity reversal beyond the stated Essex clause, or unsafe automatic surgery recommendation found in the reviewed pool. Fragment count alone is correctly separated from partial/whole-head morphology and reconstructibility. Foundational classification/anatomy items remain, with meaningful fat-pad limits, pediatric alignment, PIN and mechanical-block scenarios. The candidate count is not treated as psychometric validation.
